newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Trade seen in range, supply fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Trade seen in range, supply fears ease.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to range trade this week as fears of a delay in shipments eased with the loading of fresh supplies from the Philippines onto a European-bound ship, vegetable oil traders said on Monday.

The MV Luctor was expected to leave the Philippines this week after loading 35,000 tonnes of coconut oil, alleviating supply concerns fuelled by the delayed arrival of another ship, MV Blue Sapphire, into the Philippines, they said.
The MV Blue Sapphire has been stuck in China but is now expected to arrive in the Philippines on June 6, traders said.
"We are in a lull... waiting for news on Sapphire and the effects of the rains in the southern Philippines," one senior trader said. "Prices will likely move in a narrow band of $5 up or down."
Coconut oil sellers quoted $642.50 per tonne C&F on Saturday against $630 for buyers, trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines said.
Coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam dropped to 15,972 tonnes as of May 23, from 19,475 tonnes in the previous week.

Talk of a possible delay of a major Philippine coconut oil shipment for June and July delivery, spurred by Sapphire's delayed arrival, had pushed up prices by $20 a tonne since May 19. The market stabilised last Thursday on news of Luctor's arrival.
Sapphire was supposed to load 35,000 tonnes of Philippine coconut oil in May before becoming stuck in China, the traders said.
"Logistics problems due to ship delays and weather conditions such as typhoons in the Philippines will determine price swings in the second half of the year," a trader said.
The Philippines is the world's largest exporter of coconut products.
Traders said domestic prices of copra and coconut oil were up slightly on Monday due a slowdown of copra arrivals to the mills.
Copra buyers quoted 9.20 pesos a kg on Monday from last week's nine while buyers quoted coconut oil at 16.50 pesos per kg from the previous 16.20.

Traders said rains in coconut growing areas in the southern Philippines in the past several days slowed the transport of copra to mills. The rainy season in the Philippines starts in May and lasts until November.
